**Indikator 5y** is a supplementary national quality indicator within the Danish Acute Surgery Database (Akut Kirurgi Databasen) that monitors the speed of acute surgical treatment for patients without life-threatening conditions. Specifically, it measures the proportion of acute surgical patients without [[non-perforation-iskaemi-bloedning]] (perforation, ischemia, or bleeding) who are operated on within six hours of arriving at the hospital, out of those operated on within a maximum of 24 hours [^src1]. 

Data collected between September 1, 2022, and August 31, 2023, reveals significant structural challenges in acute surgical capacity and triage across Denmark [^src1]. During this period, there were 2,000 patients who met the criteria for Indikator 5y [^src1]. Of these, only 294 were operated on within the six-hour target window, resulting in a national compliance rate of just 14.7% (95% CI: 13.2-16.3) [^src1]. Consequently, the national standard of ≥ 90% was not met [^src1]. 

The shortfall was universal, with none of the reporting units fulfilling the standard during the measurement period [^src1]. Regionally, compliance rates varied, ranging from a low of 9.0% in [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] to a high of 19.9% in [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] [^src1]. Alongside its counterpart Indikator 5x, which tracks life-threatening conditions, Indikator 5y highlights a systemic inability to meet established time-to-surgery benchmarks for non-critical acute surgical interventions nationwide.
